data.title: Deflazacort
data.summary: VII Systemic corticosteroids · Intermediate-acting oxazoline derivative of prednisolone (prodrug)
data.body:
_Oral · VII Systemic corticosteroids_

**Class:** Intermediate-acting oxazoline derivative of prednisolone (prodrug)

## Mechanism of action
- Converted to its active metabolite (21-desacetyl-deflazacort), which acts on the glucocorticoid receptor like prednisolone

## Pharmacokinetics
- Rapidly absorbed and activated; half-life of the active metabolite about 1–2 h but biological effect 12–36 h
- Equivalence: 6 mg deflazacort ≈ 5 mg prednisolone (ratio about 1.2 : 1)
- Little mineralocorticoid effect

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Same indications as prednisolone — used in India as an alternative in children and patients with diabetes or bone loss concerns
- Approved in the USA for Duchenne muscular dystrophy

## Dose & formulations
- Usual 0.5–1.2 mg/kg/day as a single morning dose (6 mg replaces 5 mg prednisolone)
- Tablets 6, 12, 18, 24, 30 mg

## Adverse effects
- Same class side effects as prednisolone
- It is claimed (in Khopkar and product data) to have fewer effects on bone, glucose and weight, but this advantage is modest and inconsistent
- Weight gain and Cushingoid features are still seen

## Contraindications
- Same as other systemic steroids

## Drug interactions
- CYP3A4 inducers lower levels; CYP3A4 inhibitors raise levels

## Monitoring
- Same as prednisolone

## Pregnancy & lactation
Limited data; prednisolone is preferred in pregnancy.

## Viva points
- 6 mg deflazacort = 5 mg prednisolone
- Claimed bone- and glucose-sparing, but it still causes the full range of steroid side effects and is more expensive (Khopkar)

## Note on sources
Deflazacort is not covered in Wolverton; Khopkar and product data were used.

_Sources: Khopkar ch.8 (Oral and injectable steroids); not covered in Wolverton 4e. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
